I think one of the most important things for any product or startup is being able to take constructive criticism and actually learn from it 

A lot of companies get too caught up in growth, and bringing in new users that they forget to listen to the people already using their product.

The people using your platform every single day are the ones who understand its problems better than anyone else, and their feedback should genuinely matter.

Not every opinion is going to be right, but being open to different perspectives and understanding where people are coming from is how you improve.

Growth shouldn't just be measured by revenue or how many new users you bring in, but also by how happy your existing users are and whether you're building something sustainable long term.

At the end of the day, correct constructive criticism doesn't always come from a place of hate at all

Strauss Zelnick’s new interview with Wall Street Journal:

- He knew the GTA 6 delay was a must-have when he was informed by Rockstar’s head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe
- Zelnick was surprised when the interviewer said they don’t have enough hits, noting that they have 15 franchises that have each sold at least 5 million units (RDR2 sold 87M units)
- He values the team’s longevity to ship games together which correlates to long-term success
- Being slavishly devoted to a schedule can lead to disastrous outcomes such pulling a game from the market after release (he’s referring to the Cyberpunk 2077 launch)
- Zelnick emphasized the game is handcrafted without using generative AI
- He finished by saying the game will be spectacularly entertaining

The GTA 6 size could’ve easily exceeded 400GB without Rockstar’s compression techniques, according to dataminer Tex2.

Rockstar uses RPF compression and more efficient audio formats, which help keep game file sizes down.

GTA 6 pre-orders are about to surpass Cyberpunk 2077, which holds the record for most pre-orders (8 million).
